Description: The domain selected for the 2024 Proof-of-Concept under HEDI is the Digital domain with a specific focus the exploration of the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modelling and simulation (M&S) enabled wargaming (WG). M&S-enabled WG provides significant advantages to military end-users by creating realistic and controlled environments in which to test and refine strategies without the risks and costs associated with live training exercises. Additionally, wargaming facilitates the evaluation of new tactics and technologies, enabling military operators to adapt to evolving warfare landscapes swiftly. The ability to replicate diverse combat situations and iterate through multiple scenarios ensures that personnel are well-versed in handling a wide range of contingencies, ultimately leading to improved mission success rates and reduced casualties. The integration of AI into M&S-enabled WG could bring transformative benefits. AI enhances the realism and complexity of simulated environments by generating dynamic and adaptive threat scenarios that evolve based on the actions of the participants. This capability ensures that military operators face unpredictable and challenging situations, closely mimicking real-world conditions. AI-driven simulations can analyse vast amounts of data in real-time, providing immediate feedback and strategic recommendations, which significantly enhances the learning experience. Furthermore, AI facilitates advanced data analytics, offering deeper insights into performance metrics and enabling more precise assessments of tactics and strategies. By incorporating AI, wargaming not only becomes more efficient and effective but also fosters innovation and continuous improvement in military training and operations, ensuring that forces are better prepared for the complexities of modern warfare.

{"id":162348,"tenderTitle":"ENHANCEMENT OF THE PHASE SPACE DENSITY OF LASER COOLED NEUTRAL STRONTIUM ATOMIC SYSTEMS - EXPRO PLUS","tenderNumber":"1-12994","tenderDescription":"To develop a system enhancement in the cold atom production rate, and reduction of the thermodynamic temperature, of atomic Strontium (Sr), using novel Magneto Optical Trap (MOT) laser cooling techniques and technologies. DescriptionThe availability of an efficient and simplified system to generate a laser cooled Sr sample, in large atom numbers at low temperature, is a key driver and project enabler for both laboratory systems and field deployable systems and those for space deployment. Laser cooled atoms are an essential resource for ultra-high stability Optical Atomic Frequency Standard (OAFS) and specifically for Sr, using the quantum forbiddenelectronic transition at 698nm. These optical systems have demonstrated performance metrics (fractional frequency stability) which are orders of magnitude superior to their laser cooled RF counterparts. This opens up experimental possibilities that cannot be realised with RF systems. An Atom Interferometer, using clouds of laser cooled Sr atoms has also been proposed, and demonstrated, in a laboratory environment. Such an instrument can measure gravitational waves, in a frequency band not possible by LISA or the ground-based systems (LIGO, VIRGO etc).This activity shall serve as a development approach for both of above mentioned applications for future space implementations. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analysis of system performance requirements and parameters leading to an OAFS and mater wave interferometry (MWI) implemented with neutral Sr - Theoretical analysis of neutral Sr atomic system and implementation of system modelling tools to explore the implementation possibilities- Develop several viable design options leading to a PDR- Trade off the design options based primarily on flux enhancement and thermodynamic temperature reduction anddesign simplification; leading to CDR - Develop manufacturing, integration and test plan to verify the performance of a breadboardunit - Roadmap the development of the Sr MOT system for specific mission scenariosProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restrictedto non-prime contractors (incl.
